title: The canonical fr-phase-executor body names a Claude-Code-only dispatch flag, and rides verbatim into every harness mirror — agent files are outside the neutrality tripwire
body:
Found during the #494 run (PR #495), journal finding `r-p1-f5` (recorded `refuted` there —
real, but out of that PR's scope; see #491 for why that label is the wrong one).

## The observation

PR #495 mirrors `plugins/super-fr/agents/fr-phase-executor.md` into
`.opencode/agent/fr-phase-executor.md`, translating the frontmatter and carrying the **body
verbatim**. The body opens with:

> Dispatch it WITHOUT `isolation: "worktree"` — fr's worktree already IS this agent's
> working copy […]
>
> If you were dispatched **with** `isolation: "worktree"`, you are in the wrong place […]
> STOP and say so — the orchestrator must re-dispatch without the flag. (A shipped hook,
> `fr-phase-executor-guard.sh`, now refuses that dispatch, so this should be unreachable;
> super-fr#420.)

`isolation: "worktree"` is a **Claude Code dispatch argument**. OpenCode has no such
argument — which is exactly why `fr-phase-executor-guard.sh` is Claude-only and why #494
scoped it out ("OpenCode has no isolation argument to refuse"). So the shipped OpenCode
agent devotes two paragraphs to telling its reader how to react to a flag that cannot exist
on their harness, and names a hook that will never fire for them.

Harmless today. But it is the **same defect class as #436's class B**, which
`fr.harness.prose.scan_prose` and `test_tripwire_skill_tool_neutrality.py` exist to close
for skills: prose naming a harness-specific mechanism as *the* way something works, copied
byte-for-byte into every harness's mirror.

## Why PR #495 did not fix it

Two reasons, both worth keeping:

- **Body byte-identity is the design** (spec §3.B), and PR #495's tests assert it. Forking
  the prose per harness at sync time is precisely what that spec's §3.C rejected for skills,
  because it turns one source into three that can disagree.
- **Agent files are not scanned.** `test_tripwire_skill_tool_neutrality.py` covers
  `plugins/super-fr/skills/*/SKILL.md` plus the two mirrors. `plugins/super-fr/agents/` is
  outside its `_SKILL_TREES`, so nothing would have caught this even if the tripwire's
  vocabulary had the right entry.

## What closing it looks like

1. **Rewrite the paragraph as a scoped clause in the canonical agent**, in the
   `**Harness — <topic>:**` shape `fr.harness.prose` already requires of skills — naming
   Claude Code (the flag, the guard hook), and stating plainly that OpenCode and Hermes have
   no isolation argument on their dispatch primitive, so there is nothing to refuse and the
   instruction does not apply. One source, correct for every reader, still byte-identical
   into the mirror.
2. **Extend the neutrality tripwire to the agents trees** — canonical
   `plugins/super-fr/agents/*.md` and the generated `.opencode/agent/*.md` — so the
   convention actually holds there. Note the mirror multiplies: after #494 one canonical
   agent generates four files, so a violation reports five times; the tripwire may want to
   report canonical-only and let the sync tripwire cover the rest.

## Decision needed first

`isolation` is a *tool argument*, not a tool name, so it does not belong in
`TOOL_VOCABULARY` as-is. Either the vocabulary grows a notion of harness-specific
*arguments*, or this particular case is handled by the clause rewrite alone (1) and the
tripwire extension (2) only guards against future tool-name leaks into agent bodies. (1)
alone is worth doing regardless and is cheap.

Related: #410 (the "adding a new harness" playbook) and #411 (extract the shared
harness_sync helper) — both are about the same seam, and this is a third instance of
"the convention exists for skills and stops at the tree boundary".
